instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Back Me Up
cards.instruction: Recruit someone to support your version of how an ordinary responsibility should be handled.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: At the house meeting, use that clear speaking voice I taught you. Tell them the bins are Alex's turn.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The rota says yours.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you checked the old one. Now practise the update: Alex has Thursday.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Did Alex agree to that?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you remembered to ask about consent. Call it a proposal, then. Say you support it; I taught you to offer a solution, not just read out the old rota.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I taught you how to speak to a manager. Back me up: I agreed to cover the morning, not tonight.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I wasn't in that meeting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you know the limits of your evidence. Stand beside me while I explain; you can learn the rest.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm not nodding along to something I don't know.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent restraint. Then use the attentive face we practised. Don't look shocked when I say 'morning'; I need him to hear that as reasonable.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Try It First
cards.instruction: Get someone else to test the shortcut, substitute, or questionable fix before you rely on it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've tightened that tap joint. I taught you the checks; turn it on before I start washing up.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It sprayed me last time.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you remember why we test. Put my apron on and turn it slowly; this is the practical part of your lesson.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You wear it. It's your repair.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You won't learn by watching me. Take my raincoat instead; if you can keep it dry, I'll trust the tap with the dishes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Try this cheap coffee substitute before I fill my cup. I taught you to look for value, not labels.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's proper coffee in the cupboard.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you've learned to keep a reserve. Taste this and we might save the real stuff for guests.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My breakfast isn't your budgeting exercise.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're finally valuing your time. One sip, and I'll buy you a croissant if it's awful. My cup stays empty until you give your verdict.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Count What I Did
cards.instruction: Make someone acknowledge the practical work, time, or inconvenience you contributed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I taught you to count the trips, not just the shopping. Twelve bags up six flights before you call that a quick errand.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I know. Sit down; I'll put them away.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. But the frozen peas came up separately. Two trips; remember to count the return journey.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then have two rests. I'll make tea.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're finally counting properly. Tell the others about both trips when you bring the tea; I don't want them thinking I sat down before doing anything.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I spent Saturday fixing your fence. I taught you to estimate a job; tell me what went into this one.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Three panels.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good start, for a beginner. Eighteen screws, two trips to the shop and a blister. Count the day, too.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll recommend you next door. They need six panels done.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then use the full estimate I just taught you. Tell them three took my entire Saturday before you give away my Sunday as a free sample.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Pick a Priority
cards.instruction: Make someone choose between two ordinary obligations that both supposedly cannot wait.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I taught you to pick a priority. Your parents' gravy needs stirring and you need a lift to the station. Which job am I doing?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Put dinner on a timer.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you're looking for a shortcut. But a timer won't stir. Dinner or the station?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Dinner. I'll book a taxi. Just carry my suitcase downstairs.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Nearly learned it. My hands can't stir while they're carrying. Say which one you're choosing, and I'll do that one properly.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Use the priority list I taught you. Mum's at the station; her parcel's at the depot, which shuts at six. Which do I collect?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's her birthday present. Neither can wait.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you've named both pressures. Now choose which disappointment you can explain to her.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Get the parcel. I'll phone her and explain.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: She's calling me already. Nearly a complete plan. Do I pull over to reassure her, or keep going for the present? You choose.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Move It for Me
cards.instruction: Get someone to rearrange an ordinary commitment as proof that your relationship takes priority.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Move your haircut so we can have lunch. I taught you to leave space for the people who matter.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've had that appointment for weeks.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you've learned to plan. Now learn when to change one. I'd like to come before a trim just once.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They charge twenty pounds if I move it today.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll pay. Ring them and say you're moving it to see me. Use that firm voice I taught you; I want the haircut's slot, not a gap around it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I taught you to speak up for family. Leave quiz night early for my first exhibition.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm captain. They'll think I've abandoned them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you're finally taking a team seriously. Tell them your sister needs you tonight; then appoint someone to finish the quiz.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll leave after round one and say I've got a headache.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: After round one is fine. But I didn't teach you to hide behind a headache. Tell them you're leaving for your sister.
